intention: A manual charge can be saved without a start battery %, and the charging module derives it from the energy and the end % the same way the Supercharger path already does.
request: Source ticket: MAG-40 — Recalculated Battery start. REQ 1 (point packCapacityKWh at the MAG-32 effective capacity) is already delivered by RM52 and changes no code; the owner confirmed keeping it as is. REQ 2 is the work: derive start_battery_pct on manual charge Create and Update, mark the derived rows so they never feed the monthly capacity job, make the field optional in the gateway, and add the field help text. Unit tests: included.

decisions.decision: REQ 1 changes no code; packCapacityKWh and LatestMeasuredCapacity stay exactly as they are
decisions.why: RM52 already delivered it. Newest-non-NULL survives a thin month; previous-month-only would fall back to the hardcoded 62.0.

decisions.decision: New start_battery_source column ('USER'|'ESTIMATED'), module-computed; capacity query adds AND start_battery_source = 'USER'
decisions.why: This table already has energy_source and price_source in that exact shape. Reusing status was rejected: status here is a user-picked dropdown, unlike on supercharger_sessions.

decisions.decision: The edit form renders a derived start % as a placeholder, not a filled value, so Update re-derives it
decisions.why: Update requires every mutable field, so a pre-filled derived value returns looking user-supplied and gets stamped USER — the exact loop RD2 prevents.

decisions.decision: A start % the user typed is never recomputed or overwritten
decisions.why: Same rule the Supercharger path already keeps. A person's own reading is never replaced by a computed guess.

decisions.decision: The optional-field text goes in the field help under the input, not a page-level card; one new ES/EN key
decisions.why: The user reads it where they type. A card at the top of the page is read once and then ignored.

decisions.decision: The internal/analytics 62-vs-75 capacity disagreement is out of scope; recorded as backlog item 31
decisions.why: Analytics may not read charging's table, so it needs a new public port. That is its own change and it moves every efficiency number already shown.

decisions.decision: Unit tests are included in this roadmap
decisions.why: The owner asked for them. They cover the derivation wiring, the start_battery_source values, and the capacity-query exclusion.

decisions.decision: RD6 reversed: the capacity fix IS in scope. charging exposes MeasuredCapacityKWh (measured or nil, never 62.0); analytics uses it and keeps its car_type map as fallback. Two new tiers, 3 and 4.
decisions.why: Returning 62.0 would be worse than the model-aware map for an unmeasured car. Moving the map into charging fails: charging may not import account, so it cannot resolve car_type.

decisions.decision: RD8's design half superseded: no capacity port, no measured-capacity wiring. The whole dead efficiency branch is deleted instead (RecentEfficiency, Efficiency, deriveEfficiency, socReadings, carTypeFor, vehicleLookup, DefaultWindow, chargingSourceLimit, capacity.go). Tiers 3 and 4 collapse into one analytics tier.
decisions.why: Nothing calls RecentEfficiency — the map's only consumer. history_test.go:146 panics saying so, and the dashboard tile reads KmPerPctCalc instead. Deleting removes the second capacity definition cheaper and with no risk.

decisions.decision: Autopilot turned ON after tier 1 archived. Tier 2 (gateway) runs next, then tier 3 (analytics), without asking between tiers.
decisions.why: The owner asked for it. Tier 1 settled the design questions the later tiers depend on, so there is less left to stop for.
